newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Wife smiles again after Yeltsin operation.
newsitem.headline: Wife smiles again after Yeltsin operation.

text.p: Naina Yeltsin, visibly relieved, said on Wednesday she could smile again after her 65-year-old husband's heart operation and was now having to hold the Russian president back from a hasty departure from hospital.
Naina, who spent seven anxious hours on Tuesday as doctors performed a quintuple heart bypass, said she was happier now.
She said all the artificial tubes had been removed from Yeltsin's body and he was half sitting up in bed and talking freely.
"There is a totally different mood today than yesterday...you feel like smiling," Naina, who had visited Yeltsin with their two daughters, told Russian television.
"In my opinion he himself feels better."
Doctors said they were surprised by the speed of Yeltsin's recovery as he reassumed control of the country from Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin less than 24 hours after surgery.
Naina echoed earlier comments by the Kremlin's spokesman that Yeltsin was itching to be let out of the Cardiology Research Centre where the operation was performed.
"He is already talking about how long he has to be in here. We understand that he wants to leave this place," Naina said.
"We will really, really hold him back," she added.
Yeltsin wants to be transferred to the elite Central Clinical Hospital, where he was treated for the earlier heart attacks which made the bypass operation all but unavoidable.
